mainTopic: A נזירות vow tied to a child's birth: miscarriage and doubt, the animal set aside, and a friend who joins the vow
overview: The משנה finishes its cases about a man who vowed to be a נזיר when a child is born to him. If his wife miscarries, the תנא קמא says he is not a נזיר. רבי שמעון says he should take on נזירות with a condition, and he adds a second conditional נזירות if a later birth follows. The גמרא explains why the משנה spells out rulings that seem obvious: 'son' is read literally, and 'child' includes any child. It then shows that the lenient ruling about a miscarriage follows רבי יהודה, who is lenient when נזירות is in doubt (the case of the heap). רבי אבא asks whether an animal set aside after a miscarriage is already holy once a son is born. This matters for shearing it and working with it, and the question stays unresolved (תיקו). Finally, בן רחומי asks אביי what a friend means when he answers 'ועלי' or 'ואני' to a vow tied to a son's birth, and his question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A miscarriage does not trigger the vow
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if the man's wife miscarries, he does not become a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If his wife miscarried, he is not a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its case of a man who vowed to be a נזיר when a child is born to him. If his wife miscarries, the vow does not take effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A miscarried baby might have been viable, so it is unclear whether his condition was met. The תנא קמא still rules that he is not a נזיר. Step 12 shows that this follows רבי יהודה, who is lenient when נזירות is in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: She miscarried
A person who has taken a vow of נזירות (no wine, no haircut, no contact with the dead)
He is not

phrases.english: His wife miscarried —
he is not a nazirite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier cases of the משנה about a vow that depends on a birth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A miscarriage does not fulfill the condition 'when I have a child,' so the man is not a נזיר.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: take on נזירות with a condition
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says that after a miscarriage the man should declare: if the baby was viable, I am a נזיר because of my vow; if not, I am a נזיר by choice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: He should say, 'If the baby was viable, I am a נזיר because I have to be. If not, I am a נזיר because I choose to be.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with the תנא קמא. Because we don't know whether the miscarried baby could have lived, he tells the man to become a נזיר anyway, with a condition that covers both options.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe the baby was fully formed and could have lived, but died from some other cause; then the vow really did take effect. To be safe, the man keeps נזירות either way. He labels it 'required' if the vow took effect and 'voluntary' if it didn't, so he never takes a false vow.

keyTerms.meaning: A viable baby, one that could have lived
An obligatory נזיר, required by the earlier vow
A voluntary נזיר, taken on freely now
And if not

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון is not saying the man is definitely a נזיר because of his vow. He is saying the man should keep נזירות out of doubt, and the condition decides why he is keeping it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: He should say:
"If it was a viable baby —
I am hereby an obligatory nazirite;
and if not —
I am hereby a voluntary nazirite."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר יֹאמַר אִם הָיָה בֶּן קַיָּימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא's ruling that a miscarriage means no נזירות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of the doubt, the man keeps נזירות with a condition: obligatory if the baby was viable, voluntary if not.

steps.title: A later birth triggers the vow
steps.stepSummary: If the wife later gives birth, the תנא קמא says the man is now a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she then gave birth again, he is a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה goes back to the תנא קמא's view. After the miscarriage, if the wife has a real birth, the man's condition is now met and he becomes a נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, the miscarriage did nothing, so the vow was still waiting. This new birth is the first real 'child,' and it triggers the נזירות.

keyTerms.meaning: She again (did something a second time)
And she gave birth

phrases.english: She gave birth again —
he is a nazirite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the תנא קמא and adds what happens after a later live birth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A live birth after a miscarriage fulfills the vow, so the man becomes a נזיר.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: a second conditional נזירות
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says that after the later birth the man keeps another נזירות and declares which of the two was obligatory.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: He should say, 'If the first baby was viable, the first נזירות was required and this one is voluntary. If not, the first was voluntary and this one is required.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון continues his approach. The man already kept one נזירות after the miscarriage, and now he keeps a second one with a condition that matches the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only one of the two births can be the one that triggered the vow. If the miscarried baby was viable, the vow was already fulfilled and this new נזירות is extra. If it wasn't viable, the first נזירות was the extra one and this one is the real obligation. Either way the obligation is covered exactly once.

keyTerms.meaning: The first one (the miscarried baby, or the first נזירות)
And this one (the current נזירות)

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא: a miscarriage does nothing, and the next live birth makes him a נזיר. רבי שמעון: keep נזירות after the miscarriage with a condition, then keep a second one after the birth, with a condition that labels one of them required and the other voluntary.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: He should say:
"If the first was a viable baby —
the first was obligatory and this one is voluntary.
phrases.notes: 'The first' here means the נזירות he kept after the miscarriage; 'this one' is the נזירות he is starting now.

phrases.english: And if not —
the first was voluntary and this one is obligatory."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר יֹאמַר אִם הָרִאשׁוֹן בֶּן קַיָּימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי שמעון's version of the later-birth case, building on his ruling in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the later birth, he keeps a second נזירות; the condition makes exactly one of the two נזירות periods the obligatory one.

steps.title: Why say that a son's birth makes him a נזיר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needed to say that a man who vowed 'when I have a son' becomes a נזיר when a son is born.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Why does the משנה need to say this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and goes back to the opening ruling of the משנה: if a man vowed to be a נזיר when he has a son, and a son is born, he is a נזיר. It asks why that even needed to be said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vow said 'son,' and a son was born, so obviously the vow takes effect. The question is shaped like a simple question, but it really challenges the משנה for saying something too obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the חכמים that explains the משנה
Why is this worth saying? (a challenge that something is obvious)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is the point of saying this?
phrases.notes: 'This' points back to the start of the משנה: he vowed to be a נזיר when a son is born, and a son was born.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the earlier part of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a man who vowed 'when I have a son' becomes a נזיר when a son is born.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling is completely obvious, so the משנה seems to be wasting words.

steps.title: It was said because of the next clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the first ruling was stated only to set up the next one: a בת, טומטום, or אנדרוגינוס does not trigger the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the next clause: if a daughter, a טומטום or an אנדרוגינוס is born, he is not a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the obvious first ruling is there to set up the next ruling, which is the one that matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's real lesson is in the next clause: if the baby is not a definite boy, the vow about a 'son' does not take effect. The first clause is written so the contrast is clear.

keyTerms.meaning: The later clause of a משנה
A baby whose gender cannot be seen
A baby with both male and female features

phrases.english: Because of the later clause:
a daughter, a tumtum, or a hermaphrodite —
he is not a nazirite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 by explaining that the first clause is there for the sake of the next one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The obvious clause is needed to set up the next clause.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first ruling seemed to be pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is there to set up the ruling that a בת, טומטום or אנדרוגינוס does not trigger a vow about a son.

steps.title: But that is obvious too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the next clause is also obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: the next clause is just as obvious, since he said 'son' and these babies are not definitely sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving the question to the next clause doesn't help if that clause also teaches nothing new. So the גמרא now has to show why the next clause is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious!

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The next clause: a בת, טומטום or אנדרוגינוס does not trigger a vow about a son.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He said 'son,' so of course a baby who is not definitely a son does not count.

steps.title: Maybe 'son' really meant any child
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that we might have thought 'son' meant any child who builds his family, so the משנה teaches that he meant only a son.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that he really meant 'when I am built up' by having a child of any kind. So the משנה teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the clause is not obvious. Someone might think that 'son' was just his way of saying 'when I have children,' and the משנה rules that out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People often say 'son' loosely to mean children in general. The משנה teaches that we take his word 'son' literally, so only a definite son triggers the vow.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken idea)
When I will be built up, meaning when my family grows
It teaches us

phrases.english: You might have said:
"When I will be built up" is what he meant,
phrases.notes: Literally 'when I am built,' meaning when I have a child of any kind and my family grows.

phrases.english: it teaches us that this is not so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rules out a mistaken idea someone could have had.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Son' might have been a loose way of saying 'any child who builds my family.'
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'son' is taken literally; a בת, טומטום or אנדרוגינוס does not trigger the vow.
steps.whatToRemember: A vow 'when I have a son' is read literally: only a definite son counts, not any child.

steps.title: The 'child' vow also seems obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that a vow 'when I have a child' is triggered by any child, and objects that this is obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And if he said, when I have a child, and so on.' That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה: if he said 'child,' even a בת, טומטום or אנדרוגינוס triggers the vow. It objects that this is obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A daughter, a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס are all children, so of course they fit the word 'child.' The גמרא asks what this ruling adds.

keyTerms.meaning: A child (of any gender)
And so on (the rest of the quote is assumed)

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אָמַר כְּשֶׁיִּהְיֶה לִי וָלָד כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: "And if he said: When I have a child," and so on.
phrases.notes: The 'and so on' stands for the rest of the משנה's line: even a daughter, a טומטום or an אנדרוגינוס makes him a נזיר.

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next ruling of the משנה and asks the same kind of 'obvious' question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a vow about a 'child' is triggered by a בת, טומטום or אנדרוגינוס.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: These are all children, so of course the vow takes effect.

steps.title: Maybe 'child' meant one that people value
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that we might have thought he meant only a child that people consider important, so the משנה teaches that any child counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that we need a child that people consider important. So the משנה teaches us that any child counts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ruling is needed. Someone might think the man meant only the kind of child people celebrate, and the משנה teaches that any child counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the opposite of the 'son' case. There we might have read his words too broadly; here we might have read 'child' too narrowly. The משנה teaches that the plain word 'child' includes every child.

keyTerms.meaning: That is considered important
Among people
We require

steps.whatToRemember: Each vow is read by its plain words: 'son' means only a definite son, and 'child' means any child at all.
steps.whyThisMatters: Together, the two answers show that the גמרא reads a vow by its actual words, and does not stretch it wider or narrow it down based on what the person might have had in mind.

phrases.english: You might have said
we require a child that is considered important among people,
it teaches us that this is not so.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא וָלָד דְּמִיחֲשַׁב בֵּינֵי אִינָשֵׁי בָּעִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rules out a mistaken idea someone could have had.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Child' might have meant only a child that people consider important, leaving out a בת, טומטום or אנדרוגינוס.
steps.terutzMaskana: Any child fulfills a vow about a 'child.'

steps.title: Whose view says a miscarriage does not make him a nazirite?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that if his wife miscarried he is not a נזיר, and asks which תנא holds this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if his wife miscarried, he is not a נזיר. Who is the one who teaches this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line from the משנה and asks whose opinion it follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A miscarried baby might have been a real, viable child, so the vow 'when I have a son' might have been fulfilled. Ruling that he is not a נזיר means we are being lenient in a case of doubt. The גמרא wants to know which תנא holds that approach.

keyTerms.meaning: She miscarried
Who is the one who teaches this?

phrases.english: If his wife miscarried, he is not a nazirite.
Who is the one who teaches this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next ruling in the משנה after the discussion of 'son' and 'child'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a doubtful fulfillment, such as a miscarriage, does not make him a נזיר.

steps.title: It is רבי יהודה, from the case of the heap
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this is רבי יהודה, who rules leniently in the case of the heap of grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי יהודה, the one who ruled about the heap of grain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this ruling follows רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Elsewhere רבי יהודה rules that if someone vows to be a נזיר on condition that a heap of grain holds a certain amount, and it becomes unclear, he is not a נזיר. A miscarriage is the same kind of doubt, so here too he is not a נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: A heap of grain
A doubt about whether one is a נזיר

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yehuda of the heap.
phrases.notes: He means רבי יהודה's ruling about someone who vowed נזירות depending on how much grain was in a heap, and it stayed unclear.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling follows רבי יהודה, who holds that a doubtful נזירות is treated leniently.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: make a conditional vow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון from the משנה: after a miscarriage, he should vow on condition, so either way he is a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: he should say, 'If the baby was viable, I am a נזיר because of my vow. And if not, I am a נזיר by choice.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's opinion from the משנה. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון does not let the man walk away from the doubt. He keeps נזירות either way, labeled as required if the baby was viable and as voluntary if it was not. This shows that רבי שמעון is strict about a doubtful נזירות.

keyTerms.meaning: A viable child, one able to live
A נזיר out of obligation, because his vow took effect
A נזיר by free choice

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: He should say:
"If it was viable,
I am hereby an obligatory nazirite,
and if not, I am hereby a voluntary nazirite."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the opposing view in the משנה, which is strict about the doubt.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After a miscarriage, he takes on נזירות conditionally: required if the baby was viable, voluntary if not.

steps.title: רבי אבא asks about a קרבן set aside after a miscarriage
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא asks רב הונא about a man who vowed 'when I have a son.' His wife miscarried, he set aside a קרבן, and then she gave birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא asked רב הונא: someone said 'I am a נזיר when I have a son.' His wife miscarried, he set aside a קרבן, and then she gave birth. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא asks a new question about the animal the man set aside after the miscarriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the miscarriage he set aside a נזיר's קרבן. Later a real son is born, so now he is certainly a נזיר. The question is what status that earlier animal has.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him
He set aside an animal as an offering
What is the law?

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא מֵרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba asked Rav Huna:
"I am hereby a nazirite when I will have a son,"
and his wife miscarried, and he set aside an offering,
and she then gave birth, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא מֵרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a new question on the miscarriage case discussed by רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the status of the קרבן set aside after the miscarriage, once a real son is later born?

steps.title: According to whom? Not רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which view the question follows. According to רבי שמעון there is no question, since he is strict about a doubtful נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom is he asking? If according to רבי שמעון, what is his question? רבי שמעון said that in a doubt about נזירות we are strict!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which opinion רבי אבא's question is based on, and rules out רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי שמעון, after the miscarriage he really had to be a נזיר, so the animal was rightly set aside for that first נזירות. It obviously cannot count for the new נזירות of the later son, so there is nothing to ask.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whose opinion?
What is his question?
To be strict

phrases.english: According to whom?

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, מַאי תִּיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: If according to Rabbi Shimon, what is his question?
But Rabbi Shimon said:
A doubt about naziriteship is treated strictly.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן? אִי אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, מַאי תִּיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the framework of רבי אבא's question by ruling out one option.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view makes רבי אבא's question meaningful.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the question could follow רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון is strict, so the animal belonged to the first, required נזירות. There is no doubt left to ask about.

steps.title: It follows רבי יהודה: is the animal holy or not?
steps.stepSummary: The question must follow רבי יהודה, who is lenient. So after the miscarriage he was not a נזיר. Did setting the animal aside make it holy anyway?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it follows רבי יהודה, who said that in a doubt about נזירות we are lenient. So the question is: is the animal holy, or not holy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אבא's question follows רבי יהודה, and states the real question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, after the miscarriage he was not a נזיר, so setting aside the animal seemed pointless. Now that a son was born, we ask: did that earlier setting aside take effect, so the animal is already holy for his נזירות? Or is it not holy, so he must set it aside again?

keyTerms.meaning: To be lenient
Holy, set aside as הקדש

phrases.english: Rather, according to Rabbi Yehuda, who said:
A doubt about naziriteship is treated leniently.
What is it: holy, or not holy?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the remaining option after ruling out רבי שמעון.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The question follows רבי יהודה. It asks whether the earlier setting aside made the animal holy, even though he was not a נזיר at that time.

steps.title: What difference does it make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: what practical difference is there? Either way he must now bring that קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges whether the question matters at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that a son was born, he is surely a נזיר and will bring this animal as his קרבן anyway. So whether it became holy earlier or only now seems to make no practical difference.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: What difference does it make?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the practical point of the question stated in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The question 'holy or not holy' from step 16.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Either way the animal will end up as his נזיר offering, so the question seems to change nothing.

steps.title: The difference: shearing it and working with it
steps.stepSummary: The difference is whether he may shear the animal's wool and use it for work before it is brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: It matters for shearing its wool and for working with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by giving a practical difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that is הקדש may not be sheared or used for work. If it became holy back when he set it aside, these things are already forbidden. If it is not yet holy, they are still allowed until he sets it aside again.

keyTerms.meaning: Shearing the wool
To work with it, using the animal for labor

phrases.english: For its shearing and for working with it.
phrases.notes: A holy animal may not be sheared or put to work, so this is where the status matters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question seemed to have no practical result, since the animal will be brought anyway.
steps.terutzMaskana: It matters whether shearing the animal and working with it are already forbidden as הקדש.

steps.title: The question stands unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finds no answer, and רבי אבא's question is left open.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the discussion without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source settles whether the animal set aside after the miscarriage became holy according to רבי יהודה. So the question of shearing it and working with it remains a doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question remains unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's ruling that after a miscarriage he is not a נזיר follows רבי יהודה (a doubtful נזירות is treated leniently). רבי שמעון is strict. רבי אבא's question only works according to רבי יהודה: did the animal set aside after the miscarriage become holy? It matters for shearing and working with it, and it stays unresolved (תיקו).
steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean the animal is holy or not holy. It means the גמרא never decided, so it stays a doubt.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רבי אבא's question with no answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether the animal set aside after the miscarriage is already holy, according to רבי יהודה, remains unresolved.

steps.title: בן רחומי's question about a friend who says 'and upon me'
steps.stepSummary: בן רחומי asks אביי whether a friend's reply 'ועלי' links his נזירות to the first man's son or to a son of his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן רחומי asked אביי: Someone said, 'I am a נזיר when I have a son,' and his friend heard and said, 'And upon me.' What is the law? Does the friend mean he is attached to the first man's words, or does he mean himself?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question starts. בן רחומי asks what a friend's short reply 'ועלי' really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first man's נזירות starts when he has a son. The friend's reply could mean 'I'll be a נזיר when you have a son' (attached to the first man's words). It could also mean 'I'll be a נזיר when I have a son' (about himself).

keyTerms.meaning: He asked of him
When I will have a son
And upon me (I accept it too)
On his statement (the first man's words)
On himself (the friend's own situation)

phrases.english: Ben Rechumi asked of Abaye:
If one said, 'I am hereby a nazir when I will have a son,'
and his friend heard and said, 'And upon me,' what is the law?
Does it mean he is going on his statement,
phrases.notes: He means: the friend becomes a נזיר when the first man has a son.

phrases.english: or does it mean about himself?
phrases.notes: He means: the friend becomes a נזיר when he himself has a son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question, after רבי אבא's question was left unanswered in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'ועלי' ties the friend's נזירות to the first man's son or to a son of his own.

steps.title: Follow-up: a friend who says 'and I'
steps.stepSummary: Even if 'ועלי' means himself, בן רחומי asks about 'ואני': is the friend talking about himself, or saying 'I love you like yourself'?
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you say that 'And upon me' means himself: if someone said, 'I am a נזיר when I have a son,' and his friend heard and said, 'And I,' what is the law? Is he talking about himself? Or maybe he means, 'I love you as much as you love yourself'?
steps.whatsHappening: בן רחומי builds a second question on top of the first one. He asks about a different reply, 'ואני'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose 'ועלי' means the friend's own son. The words 'ואני' could still be different. They might mean 'I'm as happy as you,' so the friend becomes a נזיר when the first man's son is born.

keyTerms.meaning: If you will say (even if you decide that...)
And I
About himself
Or perhaps
I love you as you love yourself

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two replies. Step 20 is about 'ועלי' ('and upon me'). This step is about 'ואני' ('and I'), which might be a friendly way of sharing the first man's joy.

phrases.english: If you say that it means about himself,
phrases.notes: This refers back to 'ועלי' from the first question.

phrases.english: if one said, 'I am hereby a nazir when I will have a son,'
and his friend heard and said, 'And I,' what is the law?
Is he speaking about himself,
or perhaps this is what he is saying:
I love you like yourself.
phrases.notes: He means: I'd be as happy as you at your son's birth, so I'll be a נזיר then too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assumes one answer to step 20 and asks a further question on a different wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'ואני' refers to the friend's own son or shows love for the first man, tying the friend to the first man's son.

steps.title: Beginning a third question about speaking face to face
steps.stepSummary: בן רחומי starts another 'if you say' layer about things said in front of the other person. The sentence continues past this section.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say that anything said in front of him...
steps.whatsHappening: בן רחומי is setting up a third layer of his question. The sentence is not finished here and goes on in the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again he uses 'אם תמצי לומר': he assumes one answer and then asks something further. This time the new detail is whether the reply was said to the first man's face.

keyTerms.meaning: Anything, everything
In front of him, to his face

phrases.english: If you say,
that anything said in front of him

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a further layer on the question about 'ואני' in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Setup for a further question about statements said to the other person's face. The question itself is finished later.
